issues.title: amneziawg-installer: One-command AmneziaWG setup for Ubuntu/Debian VPS (3.1 by default since v6.0.0)
issues.body:
[[AmneziaWG](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amneziawg-go)](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amneziawg-go) has been discussed here before (#223, #88), but deploying it on a VPS still requires significant manual effort: building the kernel module, configuring obfuscation parameters, setting up firewall rules, and managing clients.

[**[amneziawg-installer](https://github.com/bivlked/amneziawg-installer)**](https://github.com/bivlked/amneziawg-installer) is a Bash toolkit that automates the full AmneziaWG 2.0 deployment on a dedicated Ubuntu (24.04 LTS / 25.10 / 26.04) or Debian (12 / 13) server in a single command. It targets users who want a working VPN on a clean minimal VPS without advanced Linux knowledge.

**What it does:**

- Installs AmneziaWG 2.0 with full protocol support (H1-H4 ranges, S1-S4 padding, I1-I5 CPS concealment packets, Jc/Jmin/Jmax junk packets); all obfuscation parameters are generated automatically
- Hardens the server: UFW deny-all + SSH rate-limit + VPN port only, Fail2Ban, sysctl hardening, IPv6 disabled by default (configurable via `--allow-ipv6`)
- Optimizes kernel and network stack based on detected hardware (RAM, CPU, NIC capabilities)
- Provides client management: add, remove, list, regenerate, backup/restore; outputs both `.conf` files and QR codes
- Survives reboots mid-install via a state machine that resumes from the last completed step
- Non-interactive mode with CLI flags for scripted deployments

**AmneziaWG 2.0 vs 1.x:**

The installer uses AmneziaWG 2.0, which adds CPS (Concealment Packet System) with tagged I1-I5 parameters and range-based H1-H4 headers, making traffic patterns significantly harder to fingerprint compared to AWG 1.x fixed values.

**Relevance to censorship circumvention:**

AmneziaWG modifies the WireGuard protocol at the packet level: randomized headers, junk packets, and variable padding make it resistant to the DPI signatures that censors use to block standard WireGuard (as reported in Russia #274, Iran #140, Turkmenistan #523). A user in Turkmenistan (#523) reported AmneziaWG surviving on the same IP for ~2 years, though with very low traffic (~500 MB/month); similar setups with higher consumption were banned. This installer removes the deployment barrier by handling the entire setup automatically.

License: MIT

issues.title: Remote getNodeInfo can time out while the initial route is converging
issues.body:
## Summary

A first remote `getNodeInfo` request can time out during startup even though the
peer becomes reachable and a later request succeeds. This was reproduced with
0.5.15 and also with 0.5.14; it is not being reported as a new 0.5.15 regression.

A peer key can already be known before the routing tree and Bloom state are
ready. If the initial NodeInfo packet is not delivered during that window, the
admin operation sends no further request and eventually returns
`timed out waiting for response` after six seconds.

This report concerns a cold, pending NodeInfo query. It does not establish a
cause for all remote timeouts or for long stalls after an established connection
goes idle, and it does not assume reliable delivery from the routing transport.

## Reproduction and observed result

A deterministic regression test uses two real Core instances and an isolated
loopback TCP peering:

1. Start one remote NodeInfo admin request before any peer, path or session
   exists. The destination's public key is already available to the fixture.
2. After the callback is registered and the first attempt has run, connect the
   two nodes. Do not prime the route with another NodeInfo request or traffic.
3. On unchanged develop, that single admin request times out after six seconds.
   With the candidate change, the same request recovers within that budget.

The self-contained regression file is
[`src/core/nodeinfo_cold_test.go`](https://github.com/Justsomebuddy/yggdrasil-go/blob/1e8bfb3d5bddf462a6037374d474d48a5f92c27a/src/core/nodeinfo_cold_test.go).
It can be copied alone into unchanged develop at
`2c7f050fc5398ecd8ac5f77e9bb5bd91aa2e9e35` and run with:

```sh
go test ./src/core -run '^TestNodeInfo(ColdStart|UnreachableBudget)$' -count=1
```

Both regression assertions fail semantically against the unchanged Core: the
cold query times out, and an unreachable destination produces one lookup with
its callback still pending, rather than three attempts and prompt cleanup.
The original six-second timeout itself is unchanged.

## Proposed bounded recovery

[Candidate diff](https://github.com/Justsomebuddy/yggdrasil-go/compare/2c7f050fc5398ecd8ac5f77e9bb5bd91aa2e9e35...1e8bfb3d5bddf462a6037374d474d48a5f92c27a)
([branch](https://github.com/Justsomebuddy/yggdrasil-go/tree/fix/nodeinfo-cold-start-retry)).

- Retry the unanswered NodeInfo query at two and four seconds, within the
  existing six-second deadline: at most three attempts, no extended timeout.
- Keep callback ownership, retry checks and cleanup on the NodeInfo actor.
- Cancel pending attempts on response, timeout or core shutdown. An older
  request cannot delete or reclaim a newer request's callback for the same key.
- Preserve local queries, response shape and the timeout error. No dependency,
  routing-library, configuration or wire-format changes.

This is request-level recovery for a read-only admin operation, not a guarantee
of delivery or a redesign of the existing last-request-per-key semantics.

## Verification

- Nine new tests passed five repetitions, plus `-race` and `go vet`, using the
  exact Linux Core sources and new tests in a file-scoped local run. That local
  run did not include the existing package-wide tests.
- The existing full-tree CI then passed all 13 jobs at head
  `1e8bfb3d5bddf462a6037374d474d48a5f92c27a`: builds/tests on Linux, Windows and
  macOS with Go 1.26 and 1.27, FreeBSD/OpenBSD cross-builds, lint and CodeQL.
  [Successful workflow](https://github.com/Justsomebuddy/yggdrasil-go/actions/runs/40877246650).
- Negative tests cover the unchanged timeout, attempt bound, cleanup, duplicate
  replies, shutdown, queued cancellation, overlapping requests and failed writes.

PR creation is currently restricted to collaborators, so the tested candidate
is linked here for maintainer review. Would this bounded NodeInfo-level recovery
be suitable, and could a maintainer open a PR from the branch if so?

issues.title: QUIC sniffer: Don't accept ClientHello with gaps in CRYPTO data
issues.body:
Chrome's chaos protection splits the QUIC ClientHello into many small CRYPTO frames and sends them out of order. With ML-KEM the hello is about 1.9 KB, so it always spans two Initial packets.

The sniffer writes CRYPTO data into a zero-filled buffer and takes `max(offset+length)` as the received length. If the first packet has both the start and the end of the hello, that length looks complete while the middle is still zeros. When the gap covers the server name, `ReadClientHello` reads a zero name length and returns success with an empty domain. Sniffing stops there, the second packet is never looked at, and the flow gets routed by IP.

Captured from Chrome 130 to `www.youtube.com`: the first Initial carries CRYPTO ranges 0-59 and 1039-1955, hello length 1955, SNI sits in the gap. With ML-KEM disabled the layout is different and sniffing works on the second packet, by luck.

Changes:
- track received CRYPTO ranges, parse only when `[0, 4+len)` is contiguous, otherwise keep reading and return `ErrProtoNeedMoreData`
- `ReadClientHello`: reject an empty HostName (RFC 6066 needs at least 1 byte)

`TestSniffQUICChromeScatteredCryptoFrames` uses the two captured packets. The first alone must give `ErrProtoNeedMoreData`, both together `www.youtube.com`. Fails without the fix.

issues.title: TUN inbound: Support "tcp/port" and "udp/port" in `autoSystemWfpBlockLeak` on Windows; "dns" covers DoT and DoQ as well
issues.body:
https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/6853#issuecomment-6492838227

"dns" in autoSystemWfpBlockLeak only blocked port 53 outside the TUN, plus the DNS Client service on Windows 11 and Server 2022 and later, so other programs' DNS over TLS (TCP 853) and DNS over QUIC (UDP 853) could still leave outside the TUN.

autoSystemWfpBlockLeak now takes:

- "tcp/<port>", "udp/<port>": connections to that port may only go through the TUN (or come from Xray itself).
- "windnsclient": Windows' DNS Client service may only connect through the TUN, except for mDNS and LLMNR. As before, this only applies from Windows 11 and Server 2022 on, where the service may use DoH or DoT to any port; earlier versions only query port 53.
- "dns": stands for "udp/53", "tcp/53", "windnsclient", "tcp/853" and "udp/853".
- "misconfigtun": unchanged.

Values are case-insensitive, deduplicated, and anything else, such as "tcp/0" or "icmp/1", is rejected. Keeping the system's DNS inside the TUN, with "udp/53", "tcp/53" or "windnsclient", needs dns to be set, as "dns" did; ports like 853 alone do not. Each port gets its own permit-through-TUN and block filters with a protocol condition, where port 53 used to have one for both protocols, and the log lists what is blocked, e.g. "[tun] blocked outside the TUN: udp/53, tcp/53, tcp/853, udp/853, windnsclient".

Tested on Windows 11 with a Wintun adapter as the outside interface: with "tcp/853", "udp/853", "tcp/7215" and "udp/7216", those are blocked outside the TUN over IPv4 and IPv6, while tcp/7216, udp/7215 and 443 are not, port 853 works through the TUN, Xray's own connections to port 853 still leave outside it, and nothing is blocked after Xray stops.

issues.title: XHTTP server: Raise HTTP/2 receive windows for faster uplink
issues.body:
## Summary

The XHTTP h1/h2 server uses `net/http`'s HTTP/2 defaults: 1 MiB receive window per connection and per stream. All uplink traffic on one h2 connection (stream-up, stream-one, and packet-up over XMUX) shares that window, so uplink is capped at ~1 MiB per RTT, about 160 Mbit/s at 50 ms RTT and lower on longer paths.

This sets `http.Server.HTTP2` to 10 MiB per connection and per stream (about 1.6 Gbit/s per connection at 52 ms RTT). Buffers are only allocated as data arrives. It's server-only, so existing clients benefit without changes. XHTTP/3 (QUIC windows) is not affected.

## Test

VLESS + XHTTP + REALITY, stock 26.10.21 client (macOS) → Linux server, 52 ms RTT, iperf3 12 s through the tunnel (Mbit/s):

| mode | up ×1 | up ×8 | down ×1 | down ×8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| stream-one, before | 76 | 171 | 156 | 367 |
| stream-one, after | 271 | 503 | 191 | 388 |
| packet-up, before | 140 | 341 | 169 | 421 |
| packet-up, after | 253 | 459 | 153 | 433 |

Download differences are within run-to-run noise; uplink improves 1.3–3.6×. (Measured with 64/16 MiB windows; the test link tops out around 500 Mbit/s, below what 10 MiB allows.)

- `go test ./transport/internet/splithttp` passes

issues.title: XHTTP transport: Accept OPTIONS as uplinkHTTPMethod
issues.body:
`uplinkHTTPMethod` accepts any method except GET outside packet-up (`infra/conf/transport_method.go`), and the client sends the configured method as is. So `"uplinkHTTPMethod": "OPTIONS"` passes config validation, but the server never processes such a request.

**Cause.** `requestHandler.ServeHTTP` answers every `OPTIONS` request with `200` right after writing the padding/CORS headers, treating it as a CORS preflight. An uplink request sent with `OPTIONS` is dropped there, so its body is never read and the session stalls.

**Change.** Treat `OPTIONS` as a preflight only when it carries `Access-Control-Request-Method`, which every browser preflight has. Any other `OPTIONS` request goes through the normal uplink handling (the existing code already treats every non-GET method as an uplink). Behaviour for POST/PUT/GET and for real preflights is unchanged. No config or protocol change; clients need no update.

**Tests** (`transport/internet/splithttp`):
- `Test_UplinkHTTPMethodOptions`: echo over packet-up, stream-up, stream-one and auto, plain and TLS, with POST, PUT and OPTIONS. Without the change OPTIONS times out or gets EOF in every mode; with it all pass (also 20x with `-race`).
- `Test_CORSPreflightStillAnswered`: a preflight with `Access-Control-Request-Method` still gets `200` and `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`.
- `Test_ServerMaxHeaderBytes`: oversized headers are rejected with 431 (this setting had no test).

Also checked end to end with real binaries: VLESS+XHTTP packet-up, `uplinkHTTPMethod: OPTIONS`, unmodified client against the patched server returns data; the same config against an unpatched server does not.

`go run ./infra/vformat/main.go -mode check -pwd ./`, `go run ./infra/vprotogen/main.go -mode check -pwd ./` and `go test ./...` pass locally (macOS arm64; the TLS cases of the new test were run with the package's arm64 skip lifted).

issues.title: uTLS: bump to 6ebdceb (Chrome 155), register hellochrome_155
issues.body:
Fixes #7131

## What

- Bump `refraction-networking/utls` from `aa6edf4` to `6ebdceb` (2026-10-06, no tagged release yet — same pinned-commit pattern as the current `aa6edf4` pin) and add `"hellochrome_155"` to `ModernFingerprints`.
- `HelloChrome_Auto` resolves to `HelloChrome_155` in uTLS 6ebdceb, so the default `chrome` preset (also used by ECH) automatically follows the current stable Chrome.

## Rationale

Per @RPRX's comment on #7131: if uTLS has not released a new tagged version by the next Xray release, bump it. As of now (2026-10-13) there is still no uTLS release containing 6ebdceb, so I'd like to land this before the next release window.

Note (per the issue): Chrome 155's ClientHello replaces the one introduced in 133; frames still on 133–154-class Chromium (e.g. Electron not yet rebased) will still emit the old Fingerprint, so `hellochrome_133`/`hellochrome_120` remain available.

## JA4 comparison (from #7131, verified by reporter)

| Source | JA4 |

> 简述：在 v26.10.17（与 main 相同）中，如果 XDRIVE 客户端在下载中途消失（进程被杀或断网），服务端无法察觉：它会继续从目标读取，并把剩余的整个响应写入存储（复现中 20 秒内写入约 235 MiB、607 个对象）。这些对象要等服务端的 mux 子连接自行结束后才会被清理（约 2.7–13 分钟），期间该会话仍被持续 LIST 轮询。原因是 XDRIVE 既没有对端存活检测，也没有背压。

Version: v26.10.17 (`92ccc93`, the newest release and the same commit as current `main`), `network: "xdrive"`, `service: "local"`. XDRIVE is only in the pre-releases since v26.9.30; it is not in v26.3.27. The session logic involved does not depend on the backend, so remote backends behave the same way.

When an XDRIVE client disappears in the middle of a download (process killed, network lost, which is common for mobile clients), the server does not notice:

1. It keeps reading from the target and writes the whole remaining response into the storage. In the repro the client had received 22 MiB of a 256 MiB body; within 20 s after the client was killed the server wrote 246,869,084 bytes in 607 objects.
2. These objects stay until the server-side mux sub-connection ends on its own: about 2.7 min when the target closes the connection after the body, about 13 min with a keep-alive target. Meanwhile the dead session is still polled (about 2 LIST per second).
3. The server logs nothing after the client is gone, even at `debug`.

With a remote backend every abandoned download can upload hundreds of MiB into the storage account, consume API quota and leave the objects there for minutes.

If only the application connection is closed while the client stays alive (curl killed), the server stops writing within about 5 s and the folder is cleaned up, so the problem is specific to the peer disappearing.

| 256 MiB body at 16 MiB/s, `sessionTtlSeconds: 30` | storage at +30 s | +90 s | +180 s | server kept writing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| download completes (control) | 0 B | 0 B | 0 B | no |
| client `kill -9` after ~2 s | 246,869,084 B / 607 objects | same | same | yes, the whole remaining body |
| client `SIGTERM` after ~2 s | 246,394,446 B / 515 objects | same | same | yes |
| curl killed, client alive | 0 B (one `.end`) | 0 B | 0 B | no, stopped within ~5 s |
| client `kill -9`, keep-alive target, watched 900 s | 246,453,796 B | same | same | yes; empty only at ~750–780 s |
| client `kill -9`, target sends `Connection: close` | 246,485,923 B | same | 0 B | yes; empty at ~165 s |

- `Listener.claim` marks the session active (`transport/internet/xdrive/xdrive.go:225`); the mark is removed only in the connection's `onClose` (`xdrive.go:234`). `collect()` skips active sessions (`xdrive.go:267-269`), so the folder of a dead session is not collected while the server-side connection is open.
- That connection is closed only when the inbound handler returns (`app/proxyman/inbound/worker.go:123-127`), i.e. after the server-side mux session ends. XDRIVE has no peer liveness signal: no heartbeat, no idle timeout. `Conn.receive` blocks on the reader channel (`conn.go:53-61`), `walReader.poll` returns quietly on an empty listing (`wal.go:295-297`), `holeTimeout` fires only when later segments exist (`wal.go:312-321`), EOF comes only from a `.end` object (`wal.go:365`).

issues.title: TLS sniffing may abandon a fragmented ClientHello before its deadline, causing routing-policy bypass and egress IP leakage
issues.body:
### Description and impact

In Xray-core v26.10.21, a valid but incomplete TLS record causes `SniffTLS()` to return `common.ErrNoClue`.

The dispatcher counts this as an unsuccessful protocol-identification attempt. Two partial reads can therefore terminate sniffing before the remaining ClientHello bytes arrive, even when the overall sniffing deadline has not expired.

**Consequence: domain-based routing can be bypassed and traffic can leak through the default outbound instead of the intended outbound. When the default outbound is direct, this exposes that outbound's public IP to the destination.** With an upstream gateway, this can expose the gateway's WAN IP instead of the intended proxy egress IP. An otherwise successful HTTPS request can therefore silently use the wrong egress.

### Controlled reproduction

Configure an inbound with TLS sniffing enabled, a domain-specific routing rule, and a different default outbound.

Compare:
1. Sending a complete ClientHello.
2. Sending a valid ClientHello in three chunks: 100 bytes, 100 bytes, then the remainder, with approximately 20 ms between chunks.

Packet capture confirmed that the third chunk arrived approximately 40 ms after the first.

Observed results over five repetitions:

| Case | Unmodified binary | Candidate patch |
|---|---|---|
| Complete ClientHello | Domain outbound: 5/5 | Domain outbound: 5/5 |
| Three-chunk ClientHello | Default outbound: 5/5 | Domain outbound: 5/5 |

### Suspected cause and candidate fix

In [common/protocol/tls/sniff.go](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/blob/v26.10.21/common/protocol/tls/sniff.go):

```diff
 headerLen := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(b[3:5]))
 if 5+headerLen > len(b) {
-    return nil, common.ErrNoClue
+    return nil, protocol.ErrProtoNeedMoreData
 }
```

The [dispatcher](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/blob/v26.10.21/app/dispatcher/default.go) already treats `ErrProtoNeedMoreData` as a reason to continue collecting data without consuming the failed-identification attempt budget.

A regression test fails before this change and passes afterward. Tests for `common/protocol/tls` and `app/dispatcher` also pass.

### Separate timeout-policy question

The dispatcher also has a 200 ms sniffing deadline. Delaying the initial ClientHello beyond that deadline can still result in default routing; the parser change above does not address this.

Would an explicit fail-closed option be appropriate, allowing sniffing timeouts to close the connection without selecting another outbound? This would allow deployments that require strict domain-based routing to reject a connection instead of silently leaking it through a default/direct outbound.

### Scope

Runtime reproduction was performed on v26.10.21. The same incomplete-record return pattern was also observed in the current main-branch source. This report does not claim runtime verification of every newer release.

The reproduction summary intentionally omits production IP addresses, credentials, private configurations, and original traffic captures.

issues.title: TUN inbound: Add `autoSystemWfpBlockLeak` on Windows (blocks "dns" and "misconfigtun" IPv4/IPv6 traffic leaks outside the TUN); Rename `autoSystemDNS` to `autoSystemDnsToGateway` on Linux (and change some behaviors)
issues.body:
Windows sends name queries to the DNS servers of all interfaces, each out through its own interface whatever the routes say, so DNS leaks past the TUN; on Windows 11 even as DNS over HTTPS or TLS, when that is set up for an interface. Other programs reach a resolver on the local network (e.g. 192.168.1.1 from DHCP) through its more specific LAN route. And an IP version that isn't routed to the TUN bypasses it entirely.

With `autoSystemWfpBlockLeak`, which needs autoSystemRoutingTable (the config is rejected otherwise), the Windows TUN now adds Windows Filtering Platform filters, all in one transaction and in a dynamic session, so that they are removed when Xray exits, even if it crashes or is killed. The option is a list, and each value blocks one kind of leak, e.g. `"autoSystemWfpBlockLeak": ["dns", "misconfigtun"]`:

* `"dns"` (needs `dns`, the config is rejected otherwise): DNS (port 53) only goes through the TUN, in both directions: its local address, and the interface it leaves or arrives by, must be the TUN's. The only exception is the DNS of the Xray process itself, which may leave through the other interfaces. On Windows 11 and Server 2022 and later, the DNS Client service may only connect through the TUN, so DoH or DoT set up for another interface cannot leave through it either; only its mDNS and LLMNR stay allowed. The filters match the service by its SID, as Windows Firewall's own rules for it do.
* `"misconfigtun"`: IPv4 or IPv6 is blocked in both directions when autoSystemRoutingTable has no route of it, the leak of a config that routes only one of them, except for the Xray process, loopback, DHCP, and for IPv6 neighbor and multicast listener discovery. Addresses don't matter: without one of a version in gateway, Windows gives the TUN a link-local one (fe80:: at once, 169.254.x.x after a few seconds), and what is routed to the TUN goes through it.

Either value works alone, e.g. `["dns"]` to block DNS leaks while an IP version stays out of the TUN on purpose; unknown values are rejected. Xray's own traffic is exempt: its connections out with a hard permit, which Windows Firewall rules do not override, connections to its inbounds with an ordinary one.

If the filters cannot be added, Xray does not start. `autoSystemWfpBlockLeak` is empty by default, so no filters are added unless it is set.

Also on Windows:

* With `"dns"`, a warning for `dns` servers outside gateway and autoSystemRoutingTable, as queries to them cannot go through the TUN and are blocked.
* While DNS is restricted and autoOutboundsInterface is in use, Xray resolves the names it would ask Windows for itself (Go's resolver on its own sockets). Those lookups, and the `localhost` DNS server whenever autoOutboundsInterface is in use (even without autoSystemWfpBlockLeak), skip the TUN's DNS servers, unless another interface uses them too, instead of looping back into the TUN.
* The DNS cache is flushed when the TUN starts and stops, and DNS registration is turned off on the TUN (through netsh before Windows 10 1809).
* Close no longer panics when registering the route or interface change callbacks failed.

On Linux, `autoSystemDNS` (XTLS/Xray-core#6773, not released yet) is renamed to `autoSystemDnsToGateway`, to match, and without an IPv4 address in gateway it now falls back to the first IPv6 one plus one. It now needs gateway (the config is rejected otherwise), and when it cannot set the system DNS, Xray does not start instead of only logging it.

The README describes all of it, and XTLS/Xray-docs-next#903 documents the options, what each system does without gateway, and `dns` in more detail.

Tested on Windows 11, elevated: that Windows accepts all the filters (amd64 and 386), and on amd64, DNS arriving through a real Wintun adapter and blocked outside it, DoH set on an adapter (per adapter, per network profile, and by global auto-upgrade) blocked outside the TUN while names still resolve through it, IPv4 and IPv6 blocked or ca

issues.body:
## Summary

This PR adds configurable XHTTP session ID generation.

Previously, XHTTP always generated session identifiers as UUID strings. This change introduces:

- `sessionIdFormat`
- `sessionIdLength`

allowing to choose alternative session ID representations and optionally use variable-length identifiers.

## Supported formats

- `uuid` (default)
- `hex`
- `base64url`
- `base32`
- `base58`
- `alnum`

## Example

```json
{
  "sessionIdFormat": "base58",
  "sessionIdLength": "16-24"
}
```

## Motivation

Some CDN providers return HTTP 403 responses when a UUID string is detected anywhere in the HTTP request.

This PR allows to select alternative session ID formats that remain unique while avoiding infrastructure-specific UUID filtering rules.

## Configuration

### UUID (existing behavior)

```json
{
  "sessionIdFormat": "uuid"
}
```

### Base58 with variable length

```json
{
  "sessionIdFormat": "base58",
  "sessionIdLength": "16-32"
}
```

### Base64URL

```json
{
  "sessionIdFormat": "base64url",
  "sessionIdLength": "20-40"
}
```

## Backward compatibility

Default behavior remains unchanged.

If `sessionIdFormat` is not specified, XHTTP continues to generate UUID session identifiers exactly as before.

Existing configurations require no changes.

issues.title: Inbound: Close and remove the handler when it fails to start
issues.body:
`inbound.Manager.AddHandler` first puts the handler into `taggedHandlers` (or `untaggedHandlers`) and, when the manager is already running, then calls `handler.Start()` and returns its error. Nothing is undone when `Start` fails.

This is the path of `HandlerService.AddInbound` (`xray api adi`). If the new inbound cannot start, for example because one of its ports is already in use, the API returns the error but the handler stays in the manager. Adding it again with the same tag fails with `existing tag found` until it is removed by hand, and the workers that did start (the ports before the busy one in a port range) keep listening.

Now a handler that fails to start is taken out of the manager again and closed, so the ports it opened are released and the tag can be used again. Startup is not affected: handlers from the config are only started later by `Manager.Start`.

Verified with the new `TestAddHandlerFailedStart`, which adds a tagged and an untagged handler whose `Start` fails to a running manager, and then adds the tag again. On main it fails with:

    handler "in" was not closed after failing to start
    handler "in" is still registered after failing to start (1 handlers)

With this change it passes. I also checked it end to end with a dokodemo-door inbound on two ports where the second one was busy: on main the first port stayed bound after the failed add, and adding the inbound again after freeing the port failed with `existing tag found: in`. With the change the first port is free again and the second add works.

Also ran `go test ./app/proxyman/inbound/...` (also with `-race`), `go test ./testing/scenarios -run TestCommander`, `go vet ./app/proxyman/inbound/...`, gofmt and `go run ./infra/vformat/main.go -mode check -pwd ./`.

issues.title: grpc: close cached clients with their outbound handler
issues.body:
Related to #7177. Requesting review of resource ownership, shutdown semantics, and API compatibility

## Problem

Outbound gRPC clients are cached by destination and MemoryStreamConfig, but core shutdown never closes or removes them. In an embedding process that stays alive, clients can retain connections and continue reconnecting after their core has stopped.

## Change

Give memory stream settings synchronous close-hook registration, and close the resources from their owning outbound handler. Register each ClientConn for exact-entry cache removal and ClientConn.Close. Refuse both reuse and creation after owner closure starts; racing creation must either register for cleanup or close its unpublished client. Cleanup runs outside the settings/cache locks, and concurrent Close callers wait for the same result.

The supported Instance lifecycle is single-start. Each fresh core retains separate ownership even when endpoint and outbound tags match. No per-run generation model, idle-timeout change or per-RPC closure of the shared ClientConn is added.

## Validation

- Synthetic regression reproduces the problem on v26.3.27 and main da2248c.
- `go test -race ./transport/internet ./transport/internet/grpc -count=1 -timeout=120s` passes on this exact branch.
- Official `go run ./infra/vformat/main.go -mode check -pwd ./` passes.
- Tests cover two live cores, sibling streams, normal/MultiMode, fresh-core cycles, failed-start cleanup, multiple destinations, owner/acquisition races, cancellation/backoff and forced dialerProxy lookup contention with Manager.Close.
- Earlier candidate testing also ran the target race suites five times and the dialerProxy test ten times. Those results are supplementary, not a claim that the whole upstream suite passes.

## Review questions / limits

- Handler.Close previously always returned nil. This candidate propagates cleanup errors. Is propagation preferred, or should transport cleanup be logged while preserving the existing return policy? Embedders must distinguish a cleanup error from a still-running core.
- MemoryStreamConfig with resource/mutex state must not be copied; direct external transport callers must close their settings.
- Manager.RemoveHandler still bypasses Handler.Close. XHTTP/nested download settings and TUN eventfd cleanup remain unfixed.
- No general multi-instance guarantee for Xray's other process-global networking state, TLS/Reality/masking matrix, or physical Android packet boundary is claimed.

This is intended as a draft for ownership/API review, not a claim that the Android product defect is resolved.

issues.title: Finalmask: Add the `lua` mask (noise's `script` moves there)
issues.body:
#7174 bolted a second Lua mask onto header-custom, which was the wrong way around. One `lua` mask covers all of it now: it is both a `tcpMasks` and a `udpMasks` entry, and the script decides what it does by the hooks it defines.

-- `HandleHeader(stream, address, role)`, TCP: a free handshake before any traffic, with `stream:Write`, `stream:Read` and `stream:Sleep`. Return a string or an error and the connection is dropped
-- `HandleHeaderWrite(header, address, role)` and `HandleHeaderRead(packet, address, role)`, UDP: prefix every packet with a header, and strip it on the other side by returning its length, or `nil` to drop the packet
-- `HandleNoise(plan, address, role)` is the old noise hook, so `noise`'s `script` is gone (it has not been in a release yet)
-- `role` is `client` or `server`, so one file serves both ends
-- a hook the script does not define is not wrapped at all: a noise only script leaves TCP connections alone and never touches a packet
-- the module is `xray.finalmask` now, with `Random` and `RandomBetween`

```json
{
    "udpMasks": [{"type": "lua", "settings": {"script": "mask.lua", "reset": "30-60"}}]
}
```

Per call it takes at most 64 noise packets and 65535 bytes of noise, 1024 bytes of header, and 65535 bytes each way in a handshake. A packet hook gets 1s, a handshake 30s. A UDP header is one Lua call per packet, the benchmarks in the package cover its cost.

The static lists can follow later, the same script can already do what they do.

issues.title: Outbound: Close the handler when removing it; VLESS Reverse Proxy: Don't start after closing
issues.body:
`outbound.Manager.RemoveHandler`, which `xray api rmo` (`HandlerService.RemoveOutbound`) calls, deletes the handler from the map but never closes it, while `inbound.Manager.RemoveHandler` does. So whatever the removed outbound's `Close()` would release keeps running:

- WireGuard creates its TUN in the constructor (a kernel TUN when available, otherwise a gVisor stack), and once used also has the device with its UDP socket and keepalives.
- VLESS with `reverse` keeps its monitor task: the removed outbound keeps dialing the server every 2 s.
- Same for MASQUE's tunnel. VLESS with `testpre` gets closed too, but its pre-connects only stop reliably with #7113: on main, `Close()` stops just the goroutines waiting to hand over a connection, not the ones redialing an unreachable server.

This shows up wherever outbounds are added and removed at runtime through the API, e.g. by panels.

### Changes

- `RemoveHandler` closes the handler it removed. It does so after releasing the manager lock, so a slow `Close()` (WireGuard) doesn't hold up `Select()`/`GetHandler()` for new connections. Removing an unknown tag still returns nil, and a removed handler is closed only once, since `Manager.Close()` no longer sees it.
- VLESS starts the reverse 2 s after the outbound is created (a goroutine in `New()`), so an outbound removed within those 2 s would still start it after `Close()`. `Reverse.Start()` is now a no-op once `Reverse.Close()` has run.

The other callers of `RemoveHandler` (commander, metrics, reverse portal, VLESS inbound's reverse) remove their own internal outbounds, whose `Close()` is a no-op or idempotent.

Connections already in flight on a removed outbound behave as before unless its `Close()` tears them down (WireGuard, MASQUE). A reverse bridge that is already connected is left to end on its own; only new ones stop.

### Reproduction (on 836a6fe)

Client: `api` with `HandlerService` behind a dokodemo-door inbound, `freedom` as the only configured outbound. Server: a plain TCP listener that only counts accepted connections.

**VLESS `reverse`**: the outbound is added with `xray api ado` and removed with `xray api rmo`. Afterwards `xray api lso` lists only the `freedom` outbound in all runs.

| `rmo` after `ado` | build | accepts at `rmo` | 3 s later | 13 s later |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 7 s | main | 3 | 4 | 9 |
| 7 s | this PR | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| 0.5 s | main | 0 | 1 | 6 |
| 0.5 s | this PR | 0 | 0 | 0 |

**WireGuard** (`noKernelTun: true`): five outbounds, each added with `ado` and removed right away with `rmo`. Goroutines from the `metrics` listener's `/debug/pprof/goroutine`: main 11 → 72, this PR 11 → 12.

### Tests

- New `TestRemoveHandlerClosesHandler` (on main the handler is closed 0 times) and `TestReverseNotStartedAfterClose` (on main the monitor runs once).
- `go test ./...` except `testing/scenarios`: the only failures also fail on main, tests that need `resources/geo*.dat` or network access.
- `go test ./testing/scenarios`: pass.
- `go run ./infra/vformat/main.go -mode check -pwd ./`: pass.

issues.title: XMC: make startup padding lengths configurable
issues.body:
```markdown
Follow-up to #6487, covering the startup-padding part of #6732.

Adds an optional `padding` array to XMC settings with configurable direction per turn:

```json
{
  "padding": [
    {"length": "44", "direction": "c2s"},
    {"length": "64-128", "direction": "s2c"},
    {"length": "25", "direction": "c2s"},
    {"length": "32768-49152", "direction": "s2c"}
  ]
}
```

Each entry specifies a fixed length or inclusive range, plus direction (`"c2s"` for client-to-server or `"s2c"` for server-to-client; full names `"client-to-server"` and `"server-to-client"` are also accepted). Turns can be in any order and direction, including consecutive same-direction turns. Both endpoints need the same array. The first length includes Login Acknowledged's two bytes; invalid ranges and directions are rejected during config loading and connection setup.

Omitting the `padding` field entirely preserves the existing 26.1.2 preset. Custom turns have no intentional delays. Data framing, keep-alives, and mask ordering are unchanged. No new dependency or wire-format change.

This deliberately leaves profile registries, version negotiation, and ongoing traffic scheduling for separate discussion. In particular, existing length checks are not a configuration-fingerprint handshake and do not detect every endpoint mismatch; the documentation calls this out.

Tests cover range validation, direction validation, prefix and VarInt boundaries, default-preset preservation, and encrypted bidirectional round trips with single, odd, and even turn counts.

issues.title: Bound shutdown after termination signal
issues.body:
This change prevents Xray from waiting indefinitely during graceful shutdown after receiving SIGTERM or interrupt.

Previously, shutdown depended on the deferred server.Close() call returning. If any feature Close() path blocked, the process could stay alive while listeners or active connections continued operating. This made stale Xray processes difficult to detect, especially when another process could bind the same port.

Now Xray runs server.Close() explicitly after receiving a termination signal and waits up to 10 seconds. If shutdown does not complete in time, the process exits with code 1 so supervisors can treat it as a failed shutdown and avoid leaving a functional stale process behind.

This issue was most visible on mobile clients. Some apps, such as Telegram proxy-style traffic, may continue using an already-established path even when the VPN/client UI appears disabled. If the old Xray process remains alive during a stuck shutdown, those connections can continue transferring traffic and updating usage counters, making the node look stopped from the client side while traffic is still flowing server-side.

issues.title: TLS : tls spoofing
issues.body:
fix #5964

### RawPacket aka TLS Spoofing

So first lets talk about the idea,

when you connect to a xray server, the censors can see your TLS ClientHello, read the SNI, and figure out what you are doing and block :)

The RawPacket aka TLS spoofing fixes that by injecting a fake TLS ClientHello before the real one Hits.


The fake one carries like a decoy domain (ex. baidu.com) and then the real one carries your actual destination (ex. www.example.com).

A sensor that captures the first packet sees baidu.com and think that you are just browsing, and everything is okay with that, but in reality your connection goes through :)


It can be configured in the `finalmask.tcp` okay? and its only for client side.


### How everything works


When Xray dials a TCP connection and the first `Write()` happens (which also triggers the real TLS handshake) , our Raw Packet setup does the following.

1.builds a fake Tls ClientHello with whatever SNI you want or you have option to provide the raw bytes (b64).

2.Then we. wrap it in a raw TCP/ip packet.

3.Then deliberately we corrupt the TCP header using whatever method is selected okay?

4. Then we shoot it out via a raw socket

5. Then immediately let the real `Write()` go through normally


In short : two packets arrive at the server back to back and the fake one gets dropped by the servers TCP stack because of the corruption and then the real handshake proceeds like nothing happened.


### Config Example

```json
{
  "streamSettings": {
    "finalmask": {
      "tcp": [
        {
          "type": "rawpacket",
          "settings": {
            "sni": "baidu.com",
            "payload": "",
            "method": "wrong-sequence",
            "ttl": 3,
            "count": 1
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```


### Available Fields

`sni` : The domain to put in the fake ClientHello. If you set this, it will auto generate a valid TLS ClientHello for you automatically. If you set `payload` and `sni` same time , sni wins here.

```
"sni": "baidu.com"
```

`payload` : If you don't want an auto gnrated ClientHello, then just encode your raw bytes that you want into base64 and put them here. I have added an option to do it from command line also. Do like this 

```
 xray tls fake-hello google.com
 ```

It will out the thing and then just copy paste.


Note : If `sni` and payload are empty or not set , the raw packet does nothing and the connection goes through normally.


`method` : It defines how we corrupt the fake packet so the server drops it.

`wrong-sequence` : It duplicates the sequence number (looks like a retransmission so server drops it)

So we grab the kernels `snd_nxt` ( the next sequence number the kernel expects to send), then subtract the length of the fake payload and then use that as the sequence number of the injected packet. The results then is a duplicate of the. last segment, so the receivers TCP stack sees it as a retransmit at best, or like out of window at worst and then drops it.


`wrong-checksum`: It flips all the bits in the TCP checksum (so server sees a bad checksum and drops it)

We build the packet with a correct checksum and then flip every bit(^0xFFFF). The receiver then validates the checksum and its wrong, so the packet goes in trash.

`wrong-ack`: It sets ACK number way outside the receive window (so server sends dup ACK then drops it)

It sets the ACK number to `rcv_nxt - window/2` and that's way outside of the receivers window, and the kernel responds with a dup ACK containing the correct sequence number, then drops it.

`wrong-md5` : This adds a fake TCP MD5 signature option and server without MD5 drops it

Here we append a TCP option with kind=19 and length=18 to the TCP header. The kind 19 is the MD5 signature option (RFC 2385), if the receiver doesn't use TCP MD5 (which is basically everything except some BGP routers), it sees an unknown option

### What changed

- `dialerProxy` now uses `browser://host:port/uuid`
- Browser Dialer URLs are collected and validated during config build
- URL validation includes host:port parsing, UUID path validation, and same-port/different-IP conflict checks
- Browser Dialer remains restricted to WebSocket and XHTTP, with XHTTP limited to `auto` / `packet-up`, and REALITY rejected
- Listener startup is now controlled by the Xray instance lifecycle:
  - start in `core.Instance.Start()`
  - stop in `core.Instance.Close()`

The change keeps the simplified non-dynamic model, but ties listener lifetime to the actual Xray instance instead of starting listeners while only parsing/building config.

issues.title: WebSocket transport: Treat normal close frames as io.EOF
issues.body:
## What this fixes

A WebSocket close frame with a normal status (1000) or no status (1005) ends the byte stream the same way a FIN does, but `connection.Read` surfaced gorilla's `*websocket.CloseError` to its callers.

VLESS and Trojan carry payload without framing, so a response copy ended with that error. `app/proxyman/outbound.Handler.Dispatch` treats every error other than `io.EOF` as a failure and calls `common.Interrupt`, which releases the data still buffered in the pipe before the inbound has read it. The client gets a short response that ends with a normal FIN - silent truncation for HTTP/1.0 responses without Content-Length, and a `websocket: close 1000 (normal)` line for every such connection.

Fix: map `websocket.IsCloseError(err, CloseNormalClosure, CloseNoStatusReceived)` to `io.EOF` in `connection.Read`. Other close codes keep their error semantics. The same wrapper is used by the XHTTP browser dialer client (`transport/internet/splithttp/browser_client.go`), so that path inherits the fix.

Fixes #7235.

## Test record

Environment: `1b1647cd` (v26.10.21), linux/amd64. The configs and scripts from the report used verbatim: target answers `HTTP/1.0 200 OK` + 65536 body bytes without Content-Length, then closes; the client fetches through an `http` inbound -> VLESS/ws outbound.

| scenario | base `1b1647cd` | with fix `bba46a28` |
|---|---|---|
| 20 sequential fetches, `GOMAXPROCS=1` | 19/20 short (15 x 0 B, 2 x 32749 B, 1 x 8171 B, 1 x 8173 B); 20 `close 1000` log lines | 20/20 complete 65536 B; 0 close lines |
| 10 rounds x 20 concurrent fetches | ~172/200 short; 200 `close 1000` log lines | 200/200 complete; 0 close lines |
| raw TCP control (same scripts) | 20/20 complete; 0 close lines | 20/20 complete |

The byte counts above are from the runs saved for this report; a second base run produced the same shape (18/20 short) with a different byte split.

Unit tests (new `connection_test.go`, real WebSocket server + the production wrapper): RED on base - close 1000 and 1005 come back as `websocket: close 1000 (normal)` / `close 1005 (no status)` instead of `io.EOF`; GREEN with the fix. A 1001 (`going away`) control asserts that other close codes stay errors, before and after.

`go test ./transport/internet/...` - 25 packages pass. `go build ./...`, `gofmt`, `go vet` clean.

Known boundary: a close frame arriving in the middle of a fragmented message still surfaces as a close error, because that payload is genuinely incomplete; only a close after a complete message is remapped, which is the reported mechanism.

issues.title: SOCKS and HTTP inbounds: support dynamic user management
issues.body:
## Problem

The `socks` and `http` inbounds keep their accounts in a `map[string]string` on
the protobuf config and read it without a lock on every handshake. Neither
implements `proxy.UserManager`, so the API refuses them:

```
$ xray api adu --server=127.0.0.1:10085 ...
proxy is not a UserManager
```

The only way to add an account is to edit the config and restart xray, which
drops every live connection on the inbound. On a gateway whose clients hold
long-running TCP sessions, adding one account resets all of them.

## What this does

A new `AccountValidator` in `proxy/http` holds the same username/password pairs,
built from the config at startup and mutable afterwards. The HTTP server owns
one and exposes it through `Validator()`; the SOCKS server takes that same
instance instead of building its own, because #3682 made a single SOCKS inbound
serve both protocols, and two separate stores would diverge on the first API
call.

Both servers then implement the five `UserManager` methods, so `adu`, `rmu` and
`inbounduser` work against them.

`main/commands/all/api/inbound_user_add.go` needed one change as well:
`extractInboundUsers` switches on the inbound protocol to find the user list,
and had no case for the two protocols that keep accounts in a map rather than in
a `Users` field.

## Why a snapshot instead of an RWMutex

Handshakes read the store constantly and the API writes to it rarely, so the
validator replaces the whole map on a write. Readers load the current one with
`atomic.Pointer.Load` and no lock; a writer clones it under a mutex and swaps the
pointer. A reader holding the old map finishes against a consistent snapshot.

An `RWMutex` would be simpler, so I measured both before settling on this
(Apple M3 Max, 13 and 1000 accounts, `-benchtime=300ms`):

| lookup | ns/op |
|---|---|
| bare config map, serial (what the handshake did before) | 5.6 |
| validator, serial | 9.3 |
| validator, `RunParallel` | 0.9-1.9 |
| RWMutex, `RunParallel` | 127-137 |

The handshake path costs about 4 ns more. Under concurrency the snapshot scales
while the RWMutex does not, since every reader writes to the same lock cache
line. `validator_bench_test.go` carries the first three rows; the RWMutex row
came from a throwaway benchmark that is not part of the diff.

## Behaviour notes

- `AddUser` on a SOCKS inbound whose `auth` is not `password` is refused. Such an
  inbound never consults accounts on the SOCKS side, so the account would do
  nothing there, while the HTTP side would immediately start demanding
  credentials from clients that send none.
- Users are addressed by e-mail and fall back to the username. Accounts loaded
  from a config file have no separate e-mail, and an operator naming a user has
  the username at hand.
- `GetUser` and `RemoveUser` match case-insensitively, as the other inbounds do
  with e-mail.

## Testing

- `proxy/http/validator_test.go` and `proxy/socks/usermanager_test.go` cover add,
  remove, duplicate usernames, the empty-username case, the copy returned by
  `GetAll`, and a concurrent read/write loop for `-race`.
- `go build ./...` passes, `gofmt` is clean, and `go test ./proxy/...` passes.
- `TestTagsCache` in `app/proxyman/outbound` fails on my machine, but it fails
  the same way on a clean `main`, so it is unrelated to this change.
- Live check on a running instance: a 20 MB download through an existing account
  ran to completion (HTTP 200, 81.7 s) while three users were added and two
  removed over the API, and the process kept its pid.
- In production on eight gateways since 2026-10-19, where accounts are added and
  removed daily without a restart.

issues.title: DNS outbound: Keep hijacked A/AAAA replies within the buffer
issues.body:
`handleIPQuery` builds the A/AAAA reply into an 8 KB buffer but doesn't limit the answer count. When a lookup returns more addresses than fit (about 495 A or 282 AAAA), the builder grows into a new slice and `b.Resize` panics, which stops the process. UDP, TCP and QUIC name servers can't return that much; DoH and `localhost` can.

Fix: keep at most 256 answers. The worst case (AAAA, longest name) is 7439 bytes.

Test: `TestHandleIPQueryManyIPs` fails on main with `slice bounds out of range [:16271] with capacity 8192`.

issues.title: Windows: core fails to start with 'The system cannot find the path specified' when the working directory contains a directory junction (regression in v26.10.21)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On Windows, Xray fails to start when the **current working directory** contains a directory junction:

```
Failed to start: main: failed to load config files: [config.json] > infra/conf/serial: failed to read config: &{Name:config.json Format:json} > The system cannot find the path specified.
```

The config file itself exists and is readable — the failure happens while Xray resolves the path of an already opened file.

### Versions

- Xray core **v26.10.21** (go1.27.3 windows/amd64) — broken
- Xray core **v26.9.30** — works (the code path described below does not exist there)

### Steps to reproduce

```bat
mkdir C:\test\target
echo {}> C:\test\target\config.json
mklink /J C:\test\link C:\test\target

cd /d C:\test\link
xray run -c config.json
```

Result:

```
Xray 26.10.21 (Xray, Penetrates Everything.) 1b1647c (go1.27.3 windows/amd64)
[Info] infra/conf/serial: Reading config: &{Name:config.json Format:json}
Failed to start: main: failed to load config files: [config.json] > infra/conf/serial: failed to read config: &{Name:config.json Format:json} > The system cannot find the path specified.
```

With the **physical** path it works:

```bat
cd /d C:\test\target
xray run -c config.json
[Info] infra/conf/serial: Reading config: &{Name:config.json Format:json}
[Warning] core: Xray 26.10.21 started
```

### Root cause

`main/confloader/external/external.go`, function `readConfigFile()` (introduced in v26.10.21):

```go
path, err := filepath.Abs(file.Name())
if err != nil {
    return nil, err
}
path, err = filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
if err != nil {
    return nil, err
}
switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
case ".jsonc", ".json", ".yml", ".yaml", ".toml", ".pb", ".protobuf":
default:
    return nil, errors.New("unsupported config file extension: ", path)
}
```

`filepath.EvalSymlinks` fails on Windows with `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND` ("The system cannot find the path specified") as soon as one component of the path is a **directory junction** (this is a Go standard library behavior, see the related golang/go report).

Notes:
- the file has already been opened successfully at this point (`os.Open(arg)` succeeded);
- the resolved path is only used for an **extension whitelist** check, so the resolution itself is not required;
- the failure is fatal and prevents the core from starting at all.

### Impact

Every user whose Xray is launched with a working directory located under a junction / symlinked directory is affected, e.g.:

- Scoop: `C:\Users\<user>\scoop\apps\<app>\current` is a junction to the versioned folder;
- Chocolatey / WinGet shim directories;
- any manually created `mklink /J` layout.

This is not only a CLI issue: for example **v2rayN** (which starts the core with `run -c config.json` and `WorkingDirectory = <install dir>\binConfigs`) becomes completely unusable after updating the bundled core to v26.10.21 — the client shows `Failed to start: main: failed to load config files: [config.json] ... The system cannot find the path specified.` and no proxy is available.

### Suggested fix

Do not let the symlink resolution failure be fatal — fall back to the unresolved path and check the extension with `filepath.Ext`:

```go
path, err := filepath.Abs(file.Name())
if err != nil {
    return nil, err
}
if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path); err == nil {
    path = resolved
}
switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
case ".jsonc", ".json", ".yml", ".yaml", ".toml", ".pb", ".protobuf":
default:
    return nil, errors.New("unsupported config file extension: ", path)
}
```

### Minimal Go reproducer for the underlying behavior

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
)

func main() {
	p, err := filepath.Abs(os.Args[1])
	fmt.Println("Abs:         ", p, err)
	r, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(p)
	fmt.Println("EvalSymlinks:", r, err)
}
```

Run it with the CWD set to a junction directory and pass a file name inside it:

```bat
cd /d C:\test\link
go run main.go config.json
`

issues.title: TUN inbound: `autoOutboundsInterface` should not set IP_BOUND_IF on IPv6 sockets on Darwin (mainly macOS)
issues.body:
Since #7173, a failed interface binding fails the dial. On Darwin (macOS and iOS), setinterface fell through from IPV6_BOUND_IF to IP_BOUND_IF on IPv6 sockets, which Darwin rejects with EINVAL. So every UDP dial failed, as Go opens a dual-stack IPv6 socket for it, and so did TCP to IPv6. TCP to IPv4 uses an IPv4 socket and kept working. Before #7173 the error was only logged.

IPV6_BOUND_IF binds the whole socket, so on a dual-stack socket it covers its IPv4 traffic as well. Set only the option of the socket's family, as sockopt_darwin.go already does for sockopt.interface. The new test binds each kind of socket to lo0.

Linux, Android and FreeBSD bind with socket-level options (SO_BINDTODEVICE, SO_SETFIB) that don't depend on the IP version. On Windows, the related case of an adapter without IPv4 or IPv6 is handled in #7214.

Fixes #7228

issues.title: REALITY: post-handshake records not imitated for empty SNI
issues.body:
### Integrity requirements

- [x] I have read all the comments in the issue template and ensured that this issue meet the requirements.
- [x] I confirm that I have read the documentation, understand the meaning of all the configuration items I wrote, and did not pile up seemingly useful options or default values.
- [x] I provided the complete config and logs, rather than just providing the truncated parts based on my own judgment.
- [x] I searched issues and did not find any similar issues.
- [x] The problem can be successfully reproduced in the latest Release

### Description

**Version:** Xray-core v26.10.21, the latest release. It bundles REALITY `83f6217`, which is the current REALITY `main`. v26.7.28 (REALITY `9234c77`) has the same code, and that's where I first noticed it. The `ServerName: sni` probe config involved has been in place since the per-SNI detection was added in REALITY `21af070` (June 2025).

### Summary

REALITY copies the target's post-handshake records (NewSessionTicket) for every name in `serverNames` except the empty one, `""`. For `""`, the startup probe `DetectPostHandshakeRecordsLens` fails before it sends anything, and the failure is silent. The key for empty SNI then gets `[]int{}`, so authenticated clients without SNI get no post-handshake records at all, even when the target sends them to a client without SNI.

This is the same mismatch [Aparecium](https://github.com/ban6cat6/aparecium) exploits (#4778), the one the post-handshake record imitation was added to fix. For connections without SNI, that fix has no effect, and Aparecium still detects them.

### Why this matters

No-SNI is a documented REALITY feature: see `serverName` in the [REALITY docs](https://xtls.github.io/en/config/transports/reality.html), which say "the server-side `serverNames` must contain an empty string `""`". It is also useful in practice right now. In Russia, connecting without SNI is one of the ways around the newer SNI-based restrictions, sometimes working better than ClientHello fragmentation, and it is easier to set up in many clients than fragmentation is. So it shouldn't be dismissed as a niche option. Users who turn it on fingerprint themselves without knowing it: they get weaker camouflage than the other names on the same inbound, with no warning. The fix is two lines, only touches the startup probe, and doesn't change behaviour for named entries.

### Cause

[`record_detect.go#L61`](https://github.com/XTLS/REALITY/blob/83f621788ca88b83179810b12baa7ae518aacb83/record_detect.go#L61) and [`#L96`](https://github.com/XTLS/REALITY/blob/83f621788ca88b83179810b12baa7ae518aacb83/record_detect.go#L96) both build the probe's config like this:

```go
uConn := utls.UClient(detectConn, &utls.Config{
	ServerName: sni, // "" for the empty entry
	NextProtos: nextProtos,
}, fingerprint)
```

uTLS refuses a ClientHello that has an empty `ServerName` while certificate verification is on ([`handshake_client.go#L53`](https://github.com/refraction-networking/utls/blob/aa6edf4b11af82e110eea845bb2983d30138d651/handshake_client.go#L53)):

```
tls: at least one of ServerName, InsecureSkipVerify or InsecureServerNameToVerify must be specified in the tls.Config
```

So `Handshake()` returns before anything is sent, and the deferred function ([`record_detect.go#L32`](https://github.com/XTLS/REALITY/blob/83f621788ca88b83179810b12baa7ae518aacb83/record_detect.go#L32)) stores `[]int{}` for `"<target>  0"`, `"<target>  1"` and `"<target>  2"`. Later, [`tls.go#L411-L419`](https://github.com/XTLS/REALITY/blob/83f621788ca88b83179810b12baa7ae518aacb83/tls.go#L411-L419) looks up that key for every authenticated connection without SNI and writes nothing. The second probe, the ChangeCipherSpec one at `#L96`, fails the same way, so `GlobalMaxCSSMsgCount` is never set for these keys either.

To check the stored values directly, I called `reality.DetectPostHandshakeRecordsLens` from a small program and dumped `GlobalPostHandshakeRecordsLens` 15 s later.

issues.title: Direct/Freedom outbound: Fix `blockDelay` for DispatchLink() inbounds such as VLESS, Hysteria, etc.
issues.body:
Regression from #6060 (958eb9e). `blackhole` waits for `buf.Copy(input, buf.Discard)` and relies on the `blockDelay` timer calling `common.Interrupt(input)` to end it. That only works for a pipe: VLESS, Hysteria and other inbounds that use `DispatchLink` pass a reader on the client connection, and `Interrupt` does nothing to it. So a blocked connection stays open until the client closes it, whatever `blockDelay` is. In our tests it was still open after 330 s, longer than `connIdle`.

Drain the input in a goroutine and return once the delay has passed or the input has ended. The inbound then closes the connection, as it does after the blackhole outbound.

`TestVlessBlockDelay` covers `blockDelay` 0 and 1 through a VLESS inbound. Both cases fail on main.

issues.title: Preserve buffered bytes before returning read errors
issues.body:
`BufferedReader.Read` discards a nonempty `MultiBuffer` whenever the underlying reader returns an error with its data. This is a valid `io.Reader` result: a local TLS 1.2 reproduction delivers an application record and `close_notify` together, and `crypto/tls.Conn` returns `4, "ping", io.EOF`. `SingleReader` preserves those bytes, but the buffered adapter returns `0, io.EOF`.

Keep the error until the buffered bytes have been consumed, including when callers switch between `Read`, `ReadAtMost`, `ReadMultiBuffer` and `WriteTo`. The cached writer flush retains its existing handling; a pending read error is returned before another underlying read.

Five regression cases cover data with EOF, mixed read methods, partial reads followed by `WriteTo`, and a non-EOF error that must be reported once without an extra read. The cases fail on the original implementation and pass after the fix.

Validation:
- Deterministic local TLS reproduction and separate-record controls pass with the fix; certificate verification remains enabled.
- Affected buffer, crypto, net, pipe, SOCKS, Shadowsocks and VMess suites pass on Windows and with `-race` on Linux: 73 leaf tests each, no failures or skips.
- Native Windows build, repository format check and `git diff --check` pass.
- Full `go vet` of these packages reports two existing unreachable-code diagnostics in `proxy/vmess/encoding/commands.go:33,67`, also reproduced on unchanged main. No new diagnostics; full vet is not green.

issues.title: sockopt.interface: when the interface does not exist, the dial silently goes unbound (can loop back into TUN)
issues.body:
### Integrity requirements

- [x] I have read all the comments in the issue template and ensured that this issue meet the requirements.
- [x] I confirm that I have read the documentation, understand the meaning of all the configuration items I wrote, and did not pile up seemingly useful options or default values.
- [x] I provided the complete config and logs, rather than just providing the truncated parts based on my own judgment.
- [x] I searched issues and did not find any similar issues.
- [x] The problem can be successfully reproduced in the latest Release

### Description

If an outbound has `streamSettings.sockopt.interface` set and that interface does not exist at dial time, Xray does not fail the dial. It logs `failed to apply socket options > failed to get interface ...` at **Info** level and opens the connection without any binding, so it follows the system routing table.

`transport/internet/system_dialer.go` (v26.10.10, lines 134-139; same in v26.9.9) only logs the error returned by `applyOutboundSocketOptions` and goes on to `dialer.DialContext`. The UDP path does the same (lines 77-81). The error itself comes from `net.InterfaceByName` in `transport/internet/sockopt_darwin.go:136-140`. From reading the source, Linux takes the same path (the error is logged, not returned); I tested macOS only.

Why this matters. A typical full-tunnel setup on a desktop routes everything into a TUN interface handled by Xray (default route split as 0.0.0.0/1 + 128.0.0.0/1 into the TUN), and binds outbounds with `sockopt.interface` so that their own sockets do not enter the TUN again. If the bound interface goes away, the fallback sends the outbound's sockets into the TUN, Xray routes them to the same outbound, and the connection loops.

We hit this loop in practice on macOS. A separate OpenVPN client provided a corporate network through its own utun interface, and the corporate subnet was routed to a freedom outbound so that it would follow that VPN's route. At night the OpenVPN client lost its connection and its utun interface was removed. From then on, every connection to the corporate subnet (including DNS queries to the corporate DNS server) entered the TUN, came back to the same outbound and entered the TUN again. When we looked, there were about 8,000 looped connections, all 16,384 ephemeral ports were in use, and other processes on the host got `EADDRNOTAVAIL` (`Can't assign requested address`) on connect until the loop was broken by restarting Xray.

In that incident the outbound had no `sockopt.interface` at all, so the loop itself is a config problem. The obvious fix is to bind the outbound to the other VPN's interface (`"interface": "utunN"`), so that it can never fall into the TUN. That does not work because of this issue: once the interface disappears, the binding is skipped and the loop is back. The only visible sign is an Info-level log line, which is hidden at the usual `warning` level.

Expected: if the interface named in `sockopt.interface` cannot be found, the dial fails (fail closed), as a bound socket does when its interface has no route. At the very least the error should be logged as a warning. A silent fallback to the routing table defeats the purpose of binding: it can send traffic into a tunnel (loop) or past it (leak).

### Reproduction Method

No server and no TUN are needed. Run Xray with the config below (interface `utun99` does not exist) and send a request through the SOCKS inbound:

```
curl --socks5-hostname 127.0.0.1:1080 http://example.com/
```

Result: HTTP 200. The log shows that the interface was not found and the connection was opened anyway; its local endpoint is the address of whatever interface the routing table chose (on our machine, the address of a TUN interface that held the default route).

For comparison, with `"interface": "en0"` the same request goes out through en0 (local endpoint is en0's address) and no error is logged.

Expected result: the connection through the outbound bound

issues.title: Sockopt: Handle single-family interface binding on Windows, including TUN inbound's `autoOutboundsInterface`
issues.body:
With `autoOutboundsInterface` selecting an IPv4-only Windows adapter, a normal IPv4 UDP dial can fail with WSAEINVAL (10022). Go creates a dual-stack socket and reports `udp6`; TUN then requires both IPv6 and IPv4 interface bindings, although IPv6 is disabled on the selected adapter. IPv6-only interfaces have the corresponding IPv4-binding failure. IPv6 TCP is also unnecessarily subjected to IPv4 binding.

Keep both bindings for dual-stack UDP. If binding fails, use the existing `BindError` classification to permit one Windows UDP socket-creation retry restricted to the resolved destination's family. The TUN helper checks `IPV6_V6ONLY` and applies IPv4 options only when the UDP socket supports both families; IPv6 TCP/IP binds only IPv6.

**Why retain dual-stack first?** Freedom's packet writer can send different destinations through one UDP socket. Binding only the initial destination's family could leave the other family unbound. This change preserves mixed-family UDP when both bindings work. A single-family retry cannot emit packets on the unsupported family, and a failure to bind the required family remains fatal. Ordinary external-controller errors are not retried. No configuration fields or public APIs change.

Related to #7160 and the [follow-up discussion on #7201](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/7201#issuecomment-6314278104); this does not claim to explain every occurrence of the original error.

### Validation

Native Windows 10/amd64 in Hyper-V, Go 1.27.2, comparing unmodified `00c0277787c84425738b5e65fe515b0473e06203` with this change. A disposable Wintun adapter was tested with both protocol bindings enabled, IPv6 disabled, and IPv4 disabled. Tests exercise the actual default dialer and TUN binding helper with local UDP/TCP echo traffic.

| Native scenario | Unmodified | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dual-stack UDP, including IPv4 and IPv6 destinations on one socket | Pass | Pass |
| IPv4-only uplink, IPv4 UDP with wildcard source | Fail | Pass |
| IPv6-only uplink, IPv6 UDP | Fail | Pass |
| IPv6-only uplink, IPv6 TCP | Fail | Pass |

IPv4-mapped destinations and explicit source addresses were also checked. Required-family failures remain fatal; restricted UDP sockets reject the opposite family without delivering its packet, and an ordinary controller denial produces exactly one attempt. Dual-stack interface bindings were read back from Winsock. The temporary adapter was removed; the existing guest core/ICS runtime, original adapters, forwarding settings and routes were preserved. This is native socket/traffic evidence, not a full TUN-ingress or throughput benchmark.

Affected package tests (`proxy/tun`, `transport/internet`, `proxy/socks`, `proxy/dns`), `go vet`, upstream `vformat`, and `git diff --check` passed. Transport tests cross-compiled for Linux/amd64 and macOS/arm64; they were not executed there. The full suite and race detector were not run locally. The native investigation fixture is kept outside the production diff.

issues.title: WireGuard kernelTun: Fix capget writing past its buffer
issues.body:
`KernelTunSupported` calls `capget` with `_LINUX_CAPABILITY_VERSION_3`. For v3 (and v2) the kernel always writes **two** `__user_cap_data_struct`, 24 bytes, one for capabilities 0-31 and one for 32-63 (see `capget(2)`). The code passes a single `unix.CapUserData`, 12 bytes, so the kernel writes 12 bytes past it, over whatever comes next on the goroutine stack.

On 64-bit this has gone unnoticed so far. On 32-bit ARM it overwrites a saved return address, and creating any WireGuard outbound kills the process. That includes `xray run -test` on a WireGuard config and every WireGuard config in Android clients on 32-bit-only phones. The panic message depends on the frame layout:

```
runtime: g 1: unexpected return pc for github.com/xtls/xray-core/common.CreateObject called from 0x18
fatal error: unknown caller pc
```
```
fatal error: traceback did not unwind completely
```
Sometimes it is a SIGSEGV inside `runtime.mallocgcSmallScanNoHeaderSC5`.

The bug came in with #3871 (2024-10-15).

### Reproduction
Samsung Galaxy A13 (SM-A135F), Android 14, 32-bit only (`armeabi-v7a`), `GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm GOARM=7 CGO_ENABLED=0`, Go 1.27.3, v26.10.21 (`1b1647c`), any WireGuard outbound, `xray run -test -c wg.json`:

| build | result |
|---|---|
| default flags | crashes 3/3 |
| `-gcflags=all=-l=4` (release workflow flags) | passes, by luck of frame layout |
| `-gcflags=github.com/xtls/xray-core/proxy/wireguard=-N` | passes, by luck of frame layout |
| default flags + this fix | passes 3/3, VLESS config also passes |

The release binaries happen not to crash because `-l=4` moves things around. `gomobile bind` builds don't pass it, so v2rayNG 2.3.14 (AndroidLibXrayLite, Go 1.27.3, the same xray commit) crashes on every WireGuard delay test and connect on these phones. Other xray-based Android clients on the same phone also crash when starting WireGuard.

### Fix
Pass a `[2]unix.CapUserData` and read `data[0].Effective` (`CAP_NET_ADMIN` is 12, so it is in the first word). `go vet` is clean for linux/amd64, arm64, 386, arm and mips.

comments.issue_title: XHTTP transport: Accept OPTIONS as uplinkHTTPMethod
comments.body:
Thanks for looking at this. Not trying to reopen, just a few facts in case they change the picture.

**Why a non-POST method matters.** Yandex Cloud CDN allows only `GET`, `HEAD` and `OPTIONS` for client requests by default; `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` are unavailable unless support enables them ([docs](https://yandex.cloud/en/docs/cdn/operations/resources/configure-http)). Behind such a CDN the default XHTTP uplink (POST) is rejected with 405. Our panel users hit exactly this.

**Why GET is not enough.**
- GET is only allowed in packet-up (`uplinkHTTPMethod can be GET only in packet-up mode`), so in stream-up / stream-one there is no uplink method left that such a CDN passes.
- GET carries the data in headers/cookies in 2–3 KiB chunks, and the server already needs `Cache-Control: no-store` for bodiless requests because they get cached. OPTIONS carries a body like POST.

**What the change does.** Today `uplinkHTTPMethod: "OPTIONS"` passes config validation, but the server answers 200 as a CORS preflight and silently drops the data. The change treats `OPTIONS` as a preflight only when `Access-Control-Request-Method` is present. Tested in packet-up, stream-up, stream-one and auto, plain and TLS. If OPTIONS is not wanted, I would rather make config validation reject it with a clear error than leave a silent failure, and can send that instead.

comments.issue_title: TLS sniffing may abandon a fragmented ClientHello before its deadline, causing routing-policy bypass and egress IP leakage
comments.body:
@Fangliding 感谢说明。我理解 sniffer 是尽力而为，不能把 SNI 识别当作不可绕过的防火墙。之前把“分段识别”和“超时后的阻断策略”放在同一个 issue 里容易混淆，这里想明确分开。

**1. 正常 TLS 记录在约 40 ms 内收齐，却提前结束识别**

补充一下实际背景：这是在正常终端访问 HTTPS 网站时发现出口与域名分流规则不一致，随后做的定位和最小复现，并非针对某个恶意来源的攻击测试。用于复现的 ClientHello 由标准 TLS 库生成，没有修改成畸形握手，也不是伪造恶意 TLS Hello。

**完整 TLS 记录被分次交付，本来就属于真实网络中允许发生的正常 TCP 行为。** [RFC 9293 §3.7](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.7) 明确说明，TCP 分段边界与应用层读写缓冲区边界没有对应保证。因此，不能因为前两次读取还不完整，就把合法 TLS 记录视作两次协议识别失败。下面的具体字节数和间隔是为了稳定复现而控制的，不是在声称它们就是故障原连接的抓包边界。

复现使用的是完整、有效且带明文 SNI 的 TLS ClientHello。为控制复现，将一条 1516 字节的 TLS 记录按下面的方式写入 TCP 流：

| 时间 | 本次数据 | 累计数据 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 约 0 ms | 100 字节 | 100 字节 |
| 约 20 ms | 100 字节 | 200 字节 |
| 约 40 ms | 1316 字节 | 1516 字节，记录完整 |

这是人为控制发送边界的最小复现，但属于 TCP 合法的分段／分次读取方式：TCP 不保证一次 Read 就交付完整 TLS 记录。这里没有非法 TLS 数据、伪造 SNI 或 ECH，也没有超过 200 ms 的嗅探期限。

具体代码路径是：已有合法 TLS 记录头，长度字段也已表明记录尚未收齐，但 `SniffTLS()` 返回 `common.ErrNoClue`；dispatcher 将前两次不完整读取累计为两次识别失败，因而在剩余数据约 40 ms 到达之前结束嗅探并进入后续路由。

建议仅将这个“已识别为 TLS、但记录尚未收齐”的分支改为 `protocol.ErrProtoNeedMoreData`。dispatcher 已有相应处理逻辑，会在原有期限内继续收集数据，而不消耗协议识别失败次数。

**这个修改不延长 200 ms 期限，不要求阻断所有无法识别的协议，也不改变真正超时后的默认行为。** 原版本与该单点修改的对照中，三段发送的 5 次测试由全部走默认出站变为全部命中域名出站；完整发送的对照保持正常。

**2. 真正超过 200 ms 后是否阻断，是独立的策略问题**

到达期限后关闭连接，还是继续按 IP／默认规则路由，确实涉及兼容性与安全策略的取舍，可以另行讨论；不应以接受这项策略为前提，才能处理上面的分段识别问题。

这条补充主要想请您单独评估第 1 项：正常 TLS 记录在既有时间预算内即可收齐时，是否应使用已有的“需要更多数据”状态，而不是提前耗尽识别次数。它与在 Freedom finalRules 按 IP／端口封锁危险服务，是不同层面的问题。

以上仅包含脱敏后的复现步骤和代码行为，没有生产地址、凭据、配置或原始流量。

Now all slot files plus both watermarks are created in a single concurrent wave (index-addressed writes, mutex-guarded first error). Ring setup drops from ~4 Drive-latency rounds to ~1, which matters because traffic bursts open new rings. > > 2. 75098023 — jump to full segments once the ring is three-quarters busy Fresh rings ramp segment size 14 KB → configured size (doubling every 8 full segments) so small or idle sessions stay cheap — inline segments ride the file description and cost one read. The downside was that a bursty fresh ring holds only 8×14 KB in flight and crawls until the ramp completes; a live 2 MB transfer over a fresh ring measured ~0.65 Mbps effective, with every multiplexed substream queued behind it. The jump-to-full-size now triggers at 75% ring occupancy instead of only at full saturation, so a bursty fresh ring widens a full ack-wave earlier instead of climbing most of the ramp ladder. A dedicated test discriminates the 75% path from the saturation path. > > 3. efeaa641 — keep the reader fetch window flat Reverts an experiment from the same series that widened the reader's fetch window (6 → up to ring depth) while the session was recently active. The extra ahead-pollers kept issuing Drive reads during idle periods with no measurable latency benefit, so the window is back to a flat fetchAhead = 6 and idle quota burn returns to baseline. > > Net effect: fresh-ring ramp-up stalls — the dominant latency contributor when bursts open new rings — are largely removed, session setup is ~4× faster, and idle poll overhead is back to baseline. comments.body:
Checked the other transports/inbounds; the XHTTP h1/h2 server is the only place left on the 1 MiB `net/http` default:

- **gRPC**: grpc-go's BDP estimator grows the windows dynamically up to 16 MiB (both sides; client-side only disabled if the user sets `initial_windows_size`).
- **MASQUE over h2**: own implementation, 6 MiB stream / 15 MiB conn.
- **QUIC-based** (XHTTP/3, Hysteria, MASQUE h3): windows come from `quicParams` / quic-go defaults (Hysteria 8/20 MiB), unaffected.
- **XHTTP h2 client** (downlink): bare `x/net/http2.Transport` → 4 MiB/stream, 1 GiB/conn.
- **WS / HTTPUpgrade / RAW / HTTP inbound**: HTTP/1.1 or raw TCP, no h2 flow control.

On memory: these are upper bounds, not allocations. The server buffers only data that the client has sent and the handler hasn't read yet. In normal relaying the handler drains it right away. The bound only matters when the outbound is slower than the client.

The Google Drive ring (#7217) does the ACK by metadata: the reader updates the description of a per-direction watermark file when its head moves, and the writer reuses a slot only once the watermark has reached seq - depth. With at most 8 slots per direction and a 60 s stall timeout, a dead client no longer leaves hundreds of objects, so #7208 is solved for the Drive ring.

what I found:
1. await() in slots.go measures slotStallTimeout from the start of each wait, not from the last watermark progress. With depth 8 a reader that moves slowly makes each wait last about 8 segments of time, so a healthy but slow reader (below roughly 70 KB/s at 512 KiB segments) is failed after 60 s. Measuring from max(start, progress) fixes it. https://github.com/Ahmad-2213/Xray-core/commit/cb7eff65736892065c94a63ecf6af84eb590a5cb

## Problem
Installing or reconfiguring a self-hosted MTProxy or Telemt service can put proxy access credentials in the application's diagnostic log when logging is enabled. Exporting the log archive can then disclose those credentials to its recipient.

Confirmed against `dev` at `7f9b7db482b8b1662b7466937e578008cbcb716e`.

## Root cause
The configure scripts intentionally return machine-readable credentials. MTProxy returns the base secret and credential-bearing Telegram links; the current Telemt script returns the base secret and empty link markers. `configureContainerWorker()` collects both stdout and stderr, then `updateContainerConfigAfterInstallation()` logs the entire buffer in the MTProxy and Telemt branches.

Qt debug messages are forwarded to `Logger`, which writes them without automatic redaction. `Logger::sensitive()` is opt-in and is not used here. `LogsController::zipAll()` includes the application log. A related Docker missing/stopped error message also dumped the same buffer.

A person with access to the local log, its console output while Logger is active, or a shared diagnostic archive can obtain proxy access credentials. This does not demonstrate unauthenticated remote log access or disclosure of SSH credentials. Application file logging is opt-in (disabled by default).

- Remove the MTProxy and Telemt raw configure-output debug statements.
- Keep the Docker missing/stopped diagnostic, without the accumulated output.
- Leave all parsing, conditional field updates, configuration formats, transport modes, secret generation, and APIs unchanged.
